I'm investigating a bug: result-level caching (whole-query cache) for groupBy queries with multiple post-aggregation metrics is broken in Druid 28.0.0. The bug likely comes from PR #11595 which touched GroupByQuery processing related to post-aggregators.

Find:
1. The file(s) implementing result level cache population/reading, e.g. CachingClusteredClient, CacheUtil, ResultLevelCacheUtil or similar - specifically code that serializes/deserializes results and handles post-aggregators.
2. Any code that combines/deduplicates multiple post-aggregators, e.g. methods like `getPostAggregators`, `getPostAgg`, `withPostAggregatorSpecs`, code that removes post-aggregators from the query and applies them afterwards (likely in GroupByQuery.java or GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.java).
3. Where post-aggregators might be merged into a list where duplicates or multiple entries get lost/misordered.

Report the exact file paths and line numbers, and quote the relevant code snippets (especially any method that modifies/collects post-aggregators and any method that re-applies them during cache read). Also check git log for recent commits mentioning post-aggregator or cache. Be very thorough.

<task id="ses_e3203ddc1ffeAD1bR95mBeDmKT" state="completed">
<task_result>
# Findings: Result-level cache bug for groupBy with multiple post-aggregators

## Root cause (identified)

**The bug is in `GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.pullFromCache(boolean isResultLevelCache)` — the post-aggregator re-application loop never increments its position counter `postPos`.** With more than one post-aggregator, every cached post-agg value is written into the *same* result-row slot (`postAggregatorStart + 0`), the remaining post-agg slots are left null, and the last post-agg's value overwrites the first. This code was introduced by PR #11595 and exists verbatim in Druid 28.0.0 / this checkout.

### Buggy code — this repo
**File:** `/data1/zhangyixiang/HuaWei/SWE-bench-FeatureEnvy-test/.tmp/opencode-swebench-xawj4qvn/testbed/processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/groupby/GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.java`
**Lines 769–775:**

```java
            if (isResultLevelCache) {
              Iterator<PostAggregator> postItr = query.getPostAggregatorSpecs().iterator();
              int postPos = 0;
              while (postItr.hasNext() && results.hasNext()) {
                resultRow.set(postAggregatorStart + postPos, results.next());   // postPos NEVER incremented!
              }
            }
```

The "left over objects" sanity check below it (lines 776–782) does not catch this, because both iterators are exhausted — the loop just discards values by repeatedly overwriting slot 0.

### Correct code (upstream Druid master, for comparison)

```java
            if (isResultLevelCache) {
              for (int postPos = 0; postPos < query.getPostAggregatorSpecs().size(); postPos++) {
                if (!results.hasNext()) {
                  throw DruidException.defensive("Ran out of objects while reading postaggs from cache!");
                }
                resultRow.set(postAggregatorStart + postPos, results.next());
              }
            }
```

---

## 1. Result-level cache population/reading files

- **`/data1/zhangyixiang/HuaWei/SWE-bench-FeatureEnvy-test/.tmp/opencode-swebench-xawj4qvn/testbed/server/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/ResultLevelCachingQueryRunner.java`**
  - Line 76/82: `CacheUtil.isPopulateResultCache(...)` / `CacheUtil.isUseResultCache(...)`
  - Line 90: `strategy.computeResultLevelCacheKey(query)`
  - Line 116: `final Function<T, Object> cacheFn = strategy.prepareForCache(true);` (serialization into cache, post-aggs *are* included)
  - Line 195: `final Function<Object, T> pullFromCacheFunction = strategy.pullFromCache(true);` (deserialization — where the bug lives)
  - Line 305: `CacheUtil.populateResultCache(...)`

- **`/data1/zhangyixiang/HuaWei/SWE-bench-FeatureEnvy-test/.tmp/opencode-swebench-xawj4qvn/testbed/server/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/client/CacheUtil.java`**
  - Lines 60–72: `computeResultLevelCacheKey`, `populateResultCache`
  - Lines 144–174: `isUseResultCache`, `isPopulateResultCache`
  - Lines 186–198: `isQueryCacheable(..., boolean bySegment)` — the `bySegment` flag added by PR #11595

- **`/data1/zhangyixiang/HuaWei/SWE-bench-FeatureEnvy-test/.tmp/opencode-swebench-xawj4qvn/testbed/server/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/client/CachingClusteredClient.java`** — segment-level caching on broker only (lines 282, 312, 546); result-level caching happens one layer up in `ResultLevelCachingQueryRunner`.

## 2. PR #11595 code (git)

Commit **`7142b0c39e` — "Enable result level cache for GroupByStrategyV2 on broker (#11595)"** (in this repo's history). Key changes:

- **`processing/.../groupby/GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.java`** (line 631–636 in current file):
  ```java
  public boolean isCacheable(GroupByQuery query, boolean willMergeRunners, boolean bySegment)
  {
    //disable segment-level cache on borker,
    //see PR https://github.com/apache/druid/issues/3820
    return willMergeRunners || !bySegment;
  }
  ```
  This enabled result-level cache for groupBy v2 on the broker — the feature that exposes the buggy loop.

- **`processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/CacheStrategy.java`**: added the 3-arg `isCacheable(QueryType, boolean, boolean bySegment)` overload (current file lines ~45–60) and `pullFromCache(boolean isResultLevelCache)` / `prepareForCache(boolean isResultLevelCache)` contract (lines 113–132, `fetchAggregatorsFromCache` at line 145).

- **`processing/.../groupby/strategy/GroupByStrategyV2.java`** line ~120: `isCacheable` delegates to the tool chest; **`server/.../client/CacheUtil.java`**: passes `bySegment` (`true` for segment cache, `false` for result cache — lines 113, 131, 151, 171).

## 3. Serialize/deserialize of results with post-aggregators (the pair of functions)

**`GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.java`**, inside `getCacheStrategy(query)` (starts line 621):

- `prepareForCache(boolean isResultLevelCache)` — **lines 683–715**. Serialization is correct; post-agg values are appended one per slot:
  ```java
  if (isResultLevelCache) {
    for (int i = 0; i < query.getPostAggregatorSpecs().size(); i++) {
      retVal.add(resultRow.get(inPos++));      // correct: inPos increments
    }
  }
  ```

- `pullFromCache(boolean isResultLevelCache)` — **lines 718–787**. Reads timestamp, dims (lines 742–758, `dimPos++` present), aggregators via `CacheStrategy.fetchAggregatorsFromCache` (lines 760–767), then the **buggy post-agg loop at lines 769–775** (quoted above). Note the contrast: dim/agg loops all advance their positions; only the post-agg loop does not.

- `computeResultLevelCacheKey` — lines 654–674: includes `.appendCacheables(query.getPostAggregatorSpecs())` (line 666), so the cache key is fine; the bug is purely in cache read.

## 4. Other post-aggregator collection/modification code (checked, not buggy)

- `GroupByQuery.java` (processing module):
  - `withPostAggregatorSpecs` — line 886–888
  - Builder `setPostAggregatorSpecs(List)` — lines 1184–1187 (`Lists.newArrayList(...)` preserves order/duplicates; duplicate *names* are rejected by `verifyOutputNames`, lines 908–913)
  - `getResultRowPostAggregatorStart()` — line 424
- `GroupingEngine.java` — post-agg application at lines 366–379 and 791–802 (correct indexing)
- `TimeseriesQueryQueryToolChest.java` line 131 and `TopNQueryQueryToolChest.java` line 148 use `withPostAggregatorSpecs(...)` for their own cache paths (timeseries/topN have their own correct loops)
- `DefaultLimitSpec.java` lines 360–375: builds a `Map<String, PostAggregator>` by name (dedup by name, only used for ordering, not caching)

## Git log evidence

- `git log --all --grep="11595"` → `7142b0c39e Enable result level cache for GroupByStrategyV2 on broker (#11595)` — the only commit matching; it introduced the faulty `while` loop, and no subsequent commit in this repo fixed it. (Upstream Druid fixed it later by replacing the loop with an indexed `for` + defensive error, as shown above.)

## Summary

| Item | Location |
|---|---|
| Bug | `processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/groupby/GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.java`, lines **769–775** (`pullFromCache`): missing `postPos++` |
| Feature exposing it | PR #11595 = commit `7142b0c39e` (result-level cache enabled for GroupByStrategyV2 on broker) |
| Cache write (correct) | same file, lines 683–715 (`prepareForCache`) |
| Cache read wiring | `server/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/ResultLevelCachingQueryRunner.java` lines 116, 195 |
| Cacheability gate | same file lines 631–636 + `CacheStrategy.java` `isCacheable(query, willMergeRunners, bySegment)` + `CacheUtil.java` lines 144–198 |

Fix: increment `postPos` per iteration (or convert to the upstream indexed `for` loop that throws if the cached entry runs out of post-agg values).
</task_result>
</task>

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.pullFromCache` (processing/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/query/groupby/GroupByQueryQueryToolChest.java:769) — the result-level-cache read loop for post-aggregators never incremented its position counter `postPos`, so with multiple post-aggs every cached value was written into slot 0 (last value wins, others become null). The loop now advances per post-aggregator and throws defensively if the cached entry is short.

Verified: `GroupByQueryQueryToolChestTest` (20/20, including the cache round-trip case with two post-aggregators) and `ResultLevelCachingQueryRunnerTest` (5/5) pass in the testbed container.
